title: Keep read requests in the plan and drain queue
summary: Reading a queued request (state Queued to Proposed) drops it from `athena plan` and `athena drain`, because `steward::queued_work` only lists state Queued. I will make the queue also include requests on the drained channels that have been read but not run, as Items with read=true, so plan and drain keep seeing them after a read.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for the plan and drain queue are added, with cargo test and clippy clean.
The fix is in how the queue is derived from job state, not in each caller.
Criteria check that read requests remain in the plan and are worked by drain.
Behavior criteria name the cargo commands to run.
One focused change to the queue selection.
A test asserts the plan is non-empty after reading, not just that nothing errors.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The goal is for operators using `athena plan` and `athena drain`: a request that has been read but not yet run stays in the plan and in the drain's queue.
'Read' means state Proposed on the steward or `ask --later` channels; jobs approved through work decisions are already listed by approved_work and must not be listed twice.

The 'default --budget 2 read none' remark is read as a symptom to check: if the room check is wrong, fix it. Otherwise it is left as is, and this change makes it harmless because unread requests stay queued.
Declined requests stay out of the queue, since they wait for a correction or close.
The default plan budget and the plan's read-by-default behavior are not changed.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test queues requests on a drained channel, runs `plan` with a budget that reads some of them (stub reader), and then shows that the read requests are still in the plan entries and in `queue()` with read=true. Run `cargo test`.
A test shows that after a plan that reads requests, `drain` still works them: they are in its queue, are not read a second time, and are run in plan order. Run `cargo test`.
A second `plan` after the first one reads requests prints the same open requests, not 'nothing is open'. The test checks this with the stub-backed plan output.

Read requests on channels other than the drained ones, jobs that are running or closed, and declined jobs do not enter the queue. A test covers each. `cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

The misleading test name `the_plan_of_a_read_job_names_a_missing_path_and_an_unresolved_referenced_job` in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs is replaced or backed by a test that really reads the job before checking its plan.
The doc comment of `queued_work` and the module text of drain.rs describe the new rule: read requests stay queued for the drain until they run or close.

out_of_scope: Changing JobState semantics or the state machine in store.rs.
Drain behavior for other channels or declined jobs.
departures: The change touches core queue selection and the drain's tests, so cost and time are slightly above the reference.
